topPRs.title: feat: faster simulations (pinned rounded fork block, all-child-safes stack sim)
topPRs.author: sbvegan
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Closes #1629. Simulations are RPC-latency bound (~800 sequential reads, ~2 min cold) and never reused Foundry's per-block RPC cache, because every run forked a new head.

- **Automatic block pinning for `simulate*` recipes.** When `FORK_BLOCK_NUMBER` is unset, `simulate`, `simulate-stack` and `simulate-stack-all-safes` fork the head rounded down to a multiple of 50 blocks (`SIM_FORK_BLOCK_ROUNDING`; `1` = latest). Runs within ~10 min reuse `~/.foundry/cache/rpc/<chain>/<block>`. The block is resolved once and exported, so every forge call in a recipe uses the same state. `sign`, `sign-stack`, `approve` and `execute` are unchanged and keep using the latest block. If the head can't be fetched, the recipe falls back to latest.
- **`just simulate-stack-all-safes <network> [task]`** (`StackedSimulator.simulateStackAllChildSafes`) simulates every nested task on every child safe in **one** forge process. For each task it takes a snapshot, runs `TaskManager.executeTask` once per child-safe path (depth-2 paths expanded; EOA and EIP-7702-delegated owners skipped), reverts after each run, then advances the stack the same way `simulate-stack` does. Each run uses the existing `VALIDATION.md` hash checks and state-diff checks. The output ends with a PASS/FAIL summary of every domain/message hash, and the command exits non-zero if any run fails. It refuses to run in `STACKED_SIGNING_MODE`.
- **Less fixed overhead.** The simulator prints the stack order itself, so `simulate-stack` and `sign-stack` no longer start a separate `listStack` forge process (~4 s per call).
- **Docs.** New `docs/FAST-SIMULATIONS.md` covers pinning, all-child-safes runs, warm-then-parallel runs, `OVERRIDE_RPC_URL`/anvil, and safety caveats. `AGENTS.md`, `README.md` and `NEW_TASK_GUIDE.md` link to it.

## Measurements

Measured locally on the eth `084`→`087` stack from #1628, at block 26430565 (before 084's approvals), with READMEs temporarily set to non-terminal and an archive RPC:

| Approach | Time |
|---|---|
| 8 separate `simulate-stack` calls at the latest block (issue baseline) | ~16 min |
| `simulate-stack-all-safes eth`, cold (7 child-safe runs across 4 tasks, all PASS) | 113 s |
| `simulate-stack-all-safes eth`, warm | 34 s |
| single `simulate-stack eth 084-… council`, warm | 11 s |

On today's stack (087 only): `simulate-stack eth` took 24 s cold and 6 s warm on the same pinned block. `simulate-stack-all-safes eth` took 9 s. Its per-child hashes match `simulate-stack eth 087-soneium-fee-vault council` exactly.

## Safety notes

- Simulated results are frozen at the pinned block, which is at most 49 blocks old. Signing paths are unchanged and always use the latest block. The docs say to re-simulate at latest (`FORK_BLOCK_NUMBER=-1`) after a related on-chain execution and before signing.
- The default publicnode RPC is not an archive node. Blocks more than ~128 behind the head return 403. Rounding by 50 stays inside that window, and the docs warn about long manual pins.
- All-child-safes mode is simulation-only. It does not change hash or state-diff validation: every child safe goes through the same `executeTask` path as a normal stacked run.

## Validation

- `forge fmt --check`, `forge build`
- `forge test --match-contract StackedSimulatorUnitTest`: 55/55 pass. This includes 4 new tests: child-path discovery, an all-child-safes nested 2-task stack that checks runs are isolated and the stack advances, a failing child safe that reverts with the summary error, and refusal in signing mode. The new fork tests need an archive RPC (CI has one). Locally I ran them with the `mainnet` alias pointed at an archive endpoint.
- Edge cases of `_pin-sim-fork-block`: unset, explicit block, `-1`, rounding `1`, invalid rounding, and an unreachable RPC (falls back to latest).
- `just simulate council` on `eth/087` with automatic pinning: the hash matches `VALIDATION.md`.
- Full `forge test` against public archive gateways (Tenderly mainnet and Sepolia): 385 passed, 2 skipped, 3 failed. All 3 failures are `setUp()` failures in integration suites that need CI-only infrastructure. `RevShareContractsUpgraderIntegration`, `SetFeeVaultConfigIntegration` and `UpdateFeeVaultRecipientIntegration` hardcode `ci-sepolia-l1-archive.optimism.io` (403 outside CI) or a local anvil on `127.0.0.1:8545`. None of them use `StackedSimulator` or the justfile.
- Template regression path: all 38 `test/tasks/example/{eth,sep,opsep}` tasks pass through `src/script/simulate-task.sh`, the same script `simulate-all-templates` uses. They ran sequentially against archive RPCs, and each run printed hashes with no errors.

## Note on `check_task_pr_simulation`

This PR changes `src/tasks/StackedSimulator.sol` (framework code, no task), so the task-PR checklist job will probably ask for the simulation checklist. No task state changes. The framework's state-diff and `VALIDATION.md` checks passed for 084–087 in every mode above.
